rationale: PINS the withheld branch of the `exports` relationship (DERIV_EXPORTS_KOT3): a compilation unit that declares NO top-level type has no module identity, so it publishes no `exports` RELATIONSHIP and says so in metadata. The ExportInfo array is untouched — pool-worker.ts:1196 forwards it and import-resolution.ts:314 GATES symbol joins on it — so the file's public surface reaches consumers through the channel that has no module identity to resolve. The forbidden relationship below is the measured pre-fix behaviour: the analyzer fell back to the FILE PATH, putting a 90-character absolute path in the source of every edge. 24 of 26 analyzer-only `exports` edges over a 120-file draw were exactly that. parallel-indexer.ts:3451 drops an export edge whose source cannot resolve to a symbol, so the rows were unreadable in a graph as well as unmatchable by the oracle. Measured on the corpus: 52 names withheld over a 200-file draw (validation/m14/results/kotlin-exports-oracle.txt).

forbidRelationships.note: task-9 KOTLIN4: a file with NO primary top-level type sources its exports at the compilation-unit identity, NOT the (file) sentinel

expectNoExportsRelationshipCount.comment: stated as a COUNT, not as an absence of a forbid, so a regression that publishes edges under any source is caught even when the source is something this file's text does not suggest

expectMetadata.comment: the three PUBLIC top-level names — noTypeFunction, noTypeProperty and publicWithoutType. internalWithoutType is withheld by VISIBILITY and is not counted here, because the counter records what the module identity withheld, not what visibility withheld; counting both would make the field answer a question nobody asks. The pin makes both rules falsifiable at once: a count of 4 means the internal declaration leaked into the published set, and a count of 2 means a public one was dropped.

expectExportInfoArray.comment: the array is the surface that survives: import-resolution.ts:314 refuses to join an imported name to a symbol unless the target file's exportsByFile set contains it, so dropping these from the array would break cross-file import resolution for this file even though the relationship channel correctly published nothing

Targets/metadata/coverage are preserved; the superseded package/root source spellings are now FORBIDDEN, so the re-pin strengthens rather than weakens the pins.]
